head: 0ca9f0c6efd4de64926ea3c2fc6a22a910f5e075
summary:
Nothing new to fix; the m1 fix (O-007) is in, it works, and the slice still matches the design.

Since 666f197, the only code change is `tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/WindowScriptParseTests.cs`. It adds a Fact, `WindowCasesIsAscii`, which fails on:
- an empty file,
- a leading UTF-8 byte-order mark (EF BB BF),
- any byte of 0x80 or above. The message names the byte, its offset and its 1-based line, counting LFs, so CRLF files are counted right.

A UTF-16 BOM (FF FE) is caught too, by the 0x80 check. The class summary no longer claims that the parse check catches non-ASCII in comments. It now cites the design's "write ASCII only" rather than `WindowCases.ps1:956`. That follows triage's correction: lines 966-977 show line 956 is about `report.json`.

What I ran:
- **Targeted tests** (WindowScriptParseTests, RigLockScopeWordingTests, SmbRigTests): 22/22 passed.
- **Mutation:** I put an em dash into the line-1333 comment and saved it as UTF-8 without a BOM. Both parse cases, 5.1 included, still passed. `WindowCasesIsAscii` failed with "byte 0xE2 at offset 73276 (line 1333)". I restored the file with `git checkout`; `git status` is clean for `tests/`.
- **Full default suite:** 374/374 passed.
- **Fitness:** all 59 rules hold.

Nothing else in the tree mentions these tests, so the change made no other statement false. No other test already checks this file for ASCII, so nothing is duplicated.

The summary slightly overstates the parse check. A character such as é inside a string comes out garbled in 5.1 without a parse error. The byte check covers every byte anyway, so nothing goes unguarded; this is prose, not a gap.

O-006 is still owed to validate-slice and needs a person.

Second round: Nothing new this round; the slice is clean.

The only reader added since 666f197 is `WindowCasesIsAscii` (WindowScriptParseTests.cs:18-31). I walked its inputs as someone trying to break it:

- **Byte check.** It reads the raw bytes, so line endings, tabs and blank lines cannot hide a byte of 0x80 or above.
- **Byte-order marks.** A UTF-8 BOM is caught twice: by the list pattern and by the 0x80 check. A UTF-16 BOM (FF FE or FE FF) is caught by the 0x80 check.
- **Empty file.** It fails with its own message.
- **Missing file or repo root.** Either one throws, so the test fails loudly rather than passing.
- **Lone CR.** A file using only CR line breaks would still be caught. Only the reported line number would be wrong, because it counts `\n`. That affects the failure message, not detection.
- **UTF-16 with no BOM.** This is the one input that passes: ASCII text in that form has every byte below 0x80. It is not a realistic save (editors write UTF-16 with a BOM), and 5.1 would read such a file very differently. I did not file it.

In the mutation run this lap, `WindowCasesIsAscii` failed on the edited line (em dash at line 1333, offset 73276), and both parse cases passed as expected. The full suite is 374/374 and Fitness holds all 59 rules. O-006 is still owed to validate-slice and needs a person with a second sign-in session.

obligations.evidence: Unchanged since the last review. `tests/window/StallRig/StallRig.csproj:17` compiles `SmbRig.cs` by link, and StallRig built outside `FsAnalyser.slnx` with 0 warnings and 0 errors. No `MachineName` identifier is left in code.
`WindowScriptParseTests.WindowCasesParses` passes under powershell.exe (Desktop) and pwsh.exe (Core) on the current tree, and `WindowCasesIsAscii` now covers comments.
`RigLockScopeWordingTests` is unchanged and passes. It feeds in the verbatim unrelated lines and scans tests/, docs/ and eng/.
SmbRigTests are 18/18 in my run. `RigLock.Take` (SmbRig.cs:184-203) is unchanged.
`SmbRig.cs:176` still holds the literal `@"Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig"`, byte-identical to before the rename. The only reference is `SmbRig.cs:51`.
It needs a second sign-in session, which the agent sandbox cannot create (spike 1). Nothing in the tree measures it, so it is still owed to validate-slice for a person to run.

`tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/WindowScriptParseTests.cs:18-31` checks for no UTF-8 BOM and no byte of 0x80 or above, naming the byte, offset and line on failure. The summary at lines 5-15 is rewritten. My em-dash mutation at line 1333 failed only this Fact, and both parse cases passed. The full suite is 374/374.

cases.evidence: Covered by a build command, not a test: StallRig builds outside the .slnx from a csproj that links `SmbRig.cs`. Unchanged since the last review.

`WindowCasesParses` parses the edited `WindowCases.ps1` under 5.1 and pwsh and checks the edition. `WindowCasesIsAscii` now covers the non-ASCII-in-comment shape that the parse check cannot see: the mutation at line 1333 failed only the byte check.
`RigLockScopeWordingTests` runs `DoesNotMatch` on the real `eng/dotnet.ps1:5`, `.gitignore:1` and `WindowCases.ps1:1985` and `:2118` lines, and scans the real files.
The 18 SmbRigTests pass using their own GUID-suffixed names (`SmbRigTests.cs:137`); `Take` is unchanged.
Deferred, and the reason still holds: the lock is still `Local\`, there is no `Global\` anywhere, and spike 1's sandbox refusal of Register-ScheduledTask stands.

drift: The design gives the doc as `docs/SL-020-scanner.md`, which does not exist. The builder edited the right file, `docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md`, without saying the design's path was wrong.

The settled `WindowCases.ps1` entry in `.taad/fitness.yaml` and `RigLockScopeWordingTests.Claim` (RigLockScopeWordingTests.cs:16-18) are the same regex written twice, and `eng/rules-parity.ps1` does not compare them. The `fitness.yaml` header says settled entries have no xUnit twin, but this one effectively has a wider one, so a pattern change must be made in both places by hand.

The default `dotnet test` suite now needs pwsh.exe (PowerShell 7) on PATH: `WindowScriptParseTests` has `InlineData("pwsh.exe", "Core")`. Before this slice, default-suite tests launched only powershell.exe.

`WindowCasesIsAscii` holds every future edit of `tests/window/WindowCases.ps1` to ASCII with no BOM. The design asked this of SL-059's own edit ("write ASCII only"), and triage then chose a permanent check. The file is ASCII today, but no document besides that test's summary records it as a standing rule for the file.
